findings.title: ACID ledger closes duplicate-transfer and crash-gap risks
findings.explanation: The design binds the scoped idempotency key and payload hash to the wire intent inside the ACID ledger, then uses the transactional outbox for downstream dispatch. This is the right failure-domain boundary for a financial API where retries, process crashes, or concurrent submissions must not create duplicate wires.

findings.title: Pre-dispatch risk and compliance gating is explicit and fail-closed
findings.explanation: The submission routes through account verification, limits, AML/KYC screening, and a real-time fraud gate before a dispatchable ledger state is created. Durable hold semantics for stale or inconclusive screening are appropriate for regulated money movement.

findings.title: Authoritative status and reconciliation path reduce settlement ambiguity
findings.explanation: The architecture exposes authoritative status reads from the ledger, preserves monotonic versions, verifies rail callbacks, and adds reconciliation for ambiguous timeouts and delayed settlement evidence. That combination is strong for user-visible transfer state correctness.

results.summary: A cohesive regulated wire-transfer design with ACID ledgering, scoped idempotency, pre-dispatch fraud and compliance gates, durable outbox/queue processing, and auditable status reconciliation.

findings.title: Fraud and compliance are handled as pre-dispatch gates
findings.explanation: The design separates real-time fraud screening from KYC/AML compliance and blocks or holds wires before dispatch when evidence is missing, stale, or negative, which is the right control flow for regulated transfers.

findings.title: Rail ambiguity is handled with reconciliation rather than blind replay
findings.explanation: Rail adapters, dispatch, and reconciliation explicitly distinguish pending, confirmed, rejected, and ambiguous outcomes, reducing the risk of duplicate settlement attempts and improving auditability.

results.summary: The architecture is broadly well aligned with petabyte-scale cloud migration, with strong support for incremental transfer, validation, monitoring, security, and controlled cutover; the main gap is incomplete rollback semantics for partially applied target writes.

findings.title: Rollback is only explicit at the routing layer
findings.explanation: The design clearly supports switching the active endpoint back to the source, but it does not fully define how to undo target-side writes that may have already been applied if cutover is rolled back after partial activation. That leaves the rollback outcome for already-migrated records ambiguous.
findings.recommendation: Specify the rollback contract for partially applied data: either keep the target inactive until a hard cutover, or document compensation/replay rules and the metadata needed to restore the previous state safely.

findings.title: Quorum-backed metadata and fencing create a coherent failure-safety model

findings.title: Ledger-first uniqueness and stock enforcement

findings.title: Conversation state is bounded and operationally manageable

findings.title: Comparator and manifest handling are consistently threaded through the workflow

findings.title: Operational freshness and lag are surfaced in the design

findings.title: Partition handling policy for the authoritative store is not explicit

Without an explicit fail-closed and retry policy, session starts or renewals could be inconsistently denied or delayed in a way that is hard to reason about for the partition constraint.
findings.recommendation: Define the exact behavior for store/region unavailability during start, heartbeat, stop, and renewal calls, including whether the system fails closed, how long it retries, and what client-visible response preserves correctness.

results.summary: The architecture covers the core surge-pricing workflow well: validated mobility ingestion, zone-aware stream aggregation, versioned pricing, cached quotes, notifications, and historical auditability. findings.title: No explicit scaling mechanism for compute expansion under sustained million-per-minute load
findings.explanation: The design names partitioning, replayable streams, and load tests, which are good foundations, but it does not state how the stream processor or pricing path scales out in response to sustained spikes so that the sub-second freshness target remains met when event volume surges. Without an explicit capacity/expansion policy, the design relies on assumptions rather than a demonstrated scaling strategy.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit autoscaling or capacity-management approach for the aggregator and pricing path, tied to lag/freshness thresholds and partition skew, so the system can expand before freshness breaches during peak traffic.

findings.explanation: The design binds the scoped idempotency key and payload hash to the wire intent inside the ACID ledger, then uses the transactional outbox for downstream dispatch. findings.explanation: The submission routes through account verification, limits, AML/KYC screening, and a real-time fraud gate before a dispatchable ledger state is created. Durable hold semantics for stale or inconclusive screening are appropriate for regulated money movement.

findings.title: Authoritative status and reconciliation path reduce settlement ambiguity
findings.explanation: The architecture exposes authoritative status reads from the ledger, preserves monotonic versions, verifies rail callbacks, and adds reconciliation for ambiguous timeouts and delayed settlement evidence. That combination is strong for user-visible transfer state correctness.

findings.title: Parallel work distribution is explicit and recoverable
findings.explanation: Separate durable queues for run generation and merge stages, plus idempotent task descriptors and manifest-backed state, make the concurrency model understandable and restart-friendly.

findings.title: Output provenance and validation are handled end to end

findings.title: Fraud and compliance are handled as pre-dispatch gates

findings.title: Rail ambiguity is handled with reconciliation rather than blind replay
